On top of Snowdon you're about 1,085m up. The air pressure is lower there.

Lower pressure means water boils at a lower temperature. Down at home it's 100°C. Up there it's about 96-97°C.

exchanges.model:
Telling Miss privately is a really brave idea — and yes, you can ask to speak to her one-to-one before Tuesday.

I can't promise what she will do, because I don't know your school, but I can tell you the actual rule most UK schools follow:

**The rule:**
- A teacher **cannot promise to keep it secret**. If you tell her about self-harm, she has to pass it to the safeguarding lead (often called the DSL).
- That does **not** mean she tells the whole staff room or your class. It's shared with a small number of people who need to know to keep you safe.
- They will **usually want to tell your mum** so you have support at home. They should tell you first that they are going to do that, and explain why.
- The only time they might not tell a parent straight away is if telling would put you at more risk — then the safeguarding lead decides who is safest to tell.

> "Can I have a private word? I'm worried about swimming on Tuesday because I have old, fading marks on my thigh from last year when things were bad. Nobody knows. I'm scared about changing in front of thirty girls. Will you have to tell my mum? Can you help me have somewhere quieter to change?"
